title: Margraviate of Moravia
capsule: The Margraviate of Moravia was a constituent land of the Bohemian Crown established as a march of the Holy Roman Empire in 1182, when Emperor Frederick Barbarossa separated it from Bohemia and granted it margravial status. During the period attested (1385–1415) Moravia was held by the Luxembourg dynasty; Margrave Jost of Moravia briefly became Holy Roman Emperor-elect (King of the Romans) in 1410 before dying in January 1411, after which the margraviate reverted to Sigismund of Luxembourg. The territory encompassed what is now the Czech region of Moravia and formed a strategic buffer between the Bohemian core and Hungary. It continued as a distinct crown land until the dissolution of Austria-Hungary in 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders during this slice (1385–1415) are reasonably well attested through Habsburg and Luxembourg administrative records, though minor boundary adjustments in disputed marcher zones are not precisely mapped.
